why: Multiple post-snapshot papers extend the range of chromatic number r for which the conjecture is verified (r≤18 at snapshot time to r≤26 and then r≤29), and a separate 2025 line of work (with an AI-human collaboration platform, ProofAtlas) reports large-r exclusion results toward the general case, e.g. analytic exclusion for r≥5446. These are case-of-the-problem results narrowing the open range, directly bearing on the stated conjecture.

found.title: A Proof of Albertson's Conjecture (Albertson's Conjecture Holds for r at Most 26)
found.note: Preprint extending the verified range to r≤26; not read.

found.title: Albertson's Conjecture for Chromatic Numbers at Most 29
found.note: Preprint/review extending the verified range to r≤29; not read.

found.title: Immersions and Albertson's Conjecture
found.note: SoCG 2025 paper proving the conjecture for graphs with chromatic number k and at most 1.4(k-1) vertices, for k sufficiently large; a restricted case of the conjecture.

found.title: Progress on Albertson's Conjecture
found.note: Preprint (Cranston) reporting verification for r≤24 and restricting possible counterexamples for r in {25,26}; not read.
